text: The Patriots fell to the Bears 30-24 in a Thursday Night Football loss that underscored one of Mike Vrabel's core pillars for team identity: the turnover differential, an area where New England is currently struggling. Caleb Williams outdueled Drake Maye in what amounts to round two between these quarterbacks, throwing two touchdown passes to lead Chicago to victory, though film review of Maye's performance and the Patriots defense from the loss revealed both bright spots and areas demanding improvement going forward. On the brighter side, running back Rhamondre Stevenson reached a career high in receiving yards and continues his pattern of doing "all the little things" for the offense, while simultaneously approaching 100 carries for the sixth consecutive season—a testament to his reliability in Vrabel's system. The loss in Chicago offered eight key takeaways for the Patriots organization to process as they head into the coming week, with turnover management emerging as perhaps the most critical adjustment needed if this team hopes to reverse its fortunes.
